sn35.73:11.1: “Is what is impermanent suffering or happiness?”—
sn35.73:13.1: “Is what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change fit to be regarded thus:
sn35.73:13.2: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”—
sn35.73:15.1: “Seeing thus, bhikkhu, the instructed noble disciple experiences revulsion towards the eye … revulsion towards the mind.
sn35.73:15.2: Experiencing revulsion, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion his mind is liberated. When it is liberated there comes the knowledge: ‘It’s liberated.’
sn35.73:15.3: He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’”
